plain.text: Rachel was jealous of her sister because she had no children. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I'll die!" Jacob was angry: "Am I in the place of God, who has kept you from having children?" Rachel gave him her servant Bilhah, who had two sons, Dan and Naphtali, whom Rachel counted as hers.

Leah, who had stopped having children, gave Jacob her servant Zilpah, who had two sons, Gad and Asher. Leah's son Reuben found some mandrake plants, thought to help with having children. Rachel asked for some, and Leah said, "Wasn't it enough that you took away my husband?" They made a bargain: Rachel took the mandrakes, and Jacob spent the night with Leah.
God listened to Leah, and she had a fifth son, Issachar, and a sixth, Zebulun. Later she had a daughter named Dinah.

Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and enabled her to have a child. She had a son and said, "God has taken away my disgrace." She named him Joseph and said, "May the LORD add to me another son."

After Joseph's birth, Jacob asked Laban to let him go home with his family. Laban said he had learned that the LORD had blessed him because of Jacob, and asked him to name his wages. Jacob asked for all the speckled, spotted and dark animals from Laban's flocks. Laban agreed, but secretly removed all such animals and sent them away. Jacob used peeled branches and selective breeding with the stronger animals, and his flocks grew large and strong. Jacob became very prosperous, with large flocks, servants, camels and donkeys.

summary.bigIdea: Rivalry and jealousy fill Jacob's household, yet God keeps building the family he promised, and Joseph is born.
points: Rachel and Leah compete for Jacob's love and for children.
God listens to Leah and, later, remembers Rachel, who has Joseph.
Laban tries to cheat Jacob, but Jacob's flocks prosper.
summary.reflection: This family was full of competition. Where do you feel tempted to compare yourself with others?
